Surfaced by adding `src/repo-graph` to ROOTS (final dark-mode branch review, Important 3). GROUP_ACCENTS' 5th/6th "overflow" hues (only reached when a repo has 5+ super-groups) — teal, chosen as a visually-distinct 5th/6th accent, not derived from any brand token. Does NOT match `tokens.color.teal` (#5e9ca3) — a different, more saturated hex, so aliasing it to that token would silently change the rendered color, not a mechanical swap: migrating it is NOT possible without changing the rendered hue. Reaches the page painted directly by the client island's `cssAlpha`/`style="background:${accent}"` sites in `src/web/client/islands/repo-graph.ts` (see that file's own GROUP_ACCENTS docstring) — with no dark counterpart, it stays this same light-toned teal in dark mode too. The other 4 GROUP_ACCENTS entries (terra/moss/sky/amber) WERE byte-identical light-mode copies of brand tokens and are now `tokens.color.*` (see project-architecture.ts's own docstring on GROUP_ACCENTS) — this and the violet entry below are the genuine residue with no token to migrate to: leaving them is a DECISION, not an oversight, and remains a real, open theme-blindness gap for the rare 5-6-group case, not something this fix closes.

Fixed decorative bevel/highlight simulating physical relief on a button/toy-device skeuomorph — represents a light source's physical shadow/gloss angle, not page ink, so it must NOT ink-derive (the ink-polarity rule: shadows/highlights simulate fixed real-world depth and would incorrectly flip polarity in dark mode if tied to the `ink` token, which itself flips near-black -> near-white). No existing shadowPalette preset matches this bevel's offset-only/inset geometry (sm/md/lg are blurred drop-shadows, not hard-edged bevel lines), and it is reused nowhere else at this exact geometry — minting a bespoke single-consumer token would relocate the literal under a name rather than solve anything. Same theme-invariant treatment already established for the paired white-highlight literal in this same boxShadow.

Toy-skin literal (Family 8, TamagotchiToy.tsx SHELLS array). Fix round 1, Important 3: this reason previously called it 'a genuine user-facing color-picker feature' in the present tense - stale. src/web/primitives/HomeCenter.tsx:8,74 records that the toy view is currently SHELVED (TamagotchiToy is still exported for a future re-enable, but its ViewToggle switcher was removed) - the component is not reachable from any live route today. Kept literal anyway because tokenizing a shell color would make a user's PICKED skin flip with the theme when the view is re-enabled, defeating the point (the same reasoning as the the retired HUD, just for a currently-unreachable surface rather than a live one). This holds even where the hex happens to coincidentally equal an existing brand token (blush=egg, sage=lcd). UNRESOLVED, not closed: `tokens.color.ink2` is painted directly on the fixed `shell.color` (TamagotchiToy.tsx:100 surface, :119 header-strip ink) and measures 1.21-1.65:1 in DARK mode across five of six shells (sage 1.207, sky 1.258, lavender 1.384, blush 1.498, butter 1.650 - all live-computed from palette.ts), with charcoal already sub-floor in LIGHT mode (1.516) the opposite direction. Not Critical (the view is shelved, so nothing renders this today) but a real defect waiting for whoever re-enables the view - do not read this entry as "the shell family is settled."

Surfaced by the Important 2 CSS_COLOR_PROP_DECL widening (final dark-mode branch review) — the allowlist key is (path, literal) with no line, so this one entry covers all `black` occurrences in this file: `.rg-host .arch-gen.stale` at RepoGraph.tsx:202 (×2 — border-color AND color both mix var(--color-amber) toward black) and `.rg-host .btn.primary:hover` at RepoGraph.tsx:543 (mixes var(--ink) 88% toward black). Both are genuine, already-reviewed `color-mix(in srgb, <token> N%, black)` sites (round-1 review specifically audited every color-mix(…, black/white) site in this file for lint-guard evasion; see the file's own inline comments at both line numbers) — the black endpoint is correct precisely BECAUSE each is mixing toward black over a background/fill that stays the lighter operand in both themes (amber solid fill at :202; a hover state whose `--cream` text stays comfortably clear of the 4.5:1 text floor in both themes — recomputed against the live palette: 15.86:1 light / 14.90:1 dark before the mix, 16.40:1 light / 11.37:1 dark after — the darken IMPROVES contrast in light and REGRESSES it in dark, but crosses the floor in neither direction, at :543), not a hardcoded literal standing in for a token.

URL-encoded ink2 (#5a4f3f, exact token value) inside a background-image: url("data:image/svg+xml,...") select-chevron SVG data URI — a CSS custom property cannot be referenced inside that string, so the color is necessarily a literal PER THEME. This is the LIGHT variant; a matching dark variant (%23adadad = ink2's dark hex) is now emitted in a duplicate rule under a prefers-color-scheme media query + a forced [data-theme=dark] block, mirroring tokens.css's own four-block theme structure — the chevron now actually follows the theme (previously it was a known, comment-flagged live defect: pinned light-only, staying beige in dark mode).
URL-encoded ink2's DARK hex (#adadad, exact token value) — the dark counterpart of the %235a4f3f entry above; see that entry's reason for the full SVG-data-URI mechanism explanation.

Fixed decorative bevel/highlight simulating physical relief on a button/toy-device skeuomorph — represents a light source's physical shadow/gloss angle, not page ink, so it must NOT ink-derive (the ink-polarity rule: shadows/highlights simulate fixed real-world depth and would incorrectly flip polarity in dark mode if tied to the `ink` token, which itself flips near-black -> near-white). No existing shadowPalette preset matches this bevel's offset-only/inset geometry (sm/md/lg are blurred drop-shadows, not hard-edged bevel lines), and it is reused nowhere else at this exact geometry — minting a bespoke single-consumer token would relocate the literal under a name rather than solve anything. Same theme-invariant treatment already established for the paired white-highlight literal in this same boxShadow.

There is no class attribute here and nothing to theme. Kept as an allowlist entry rather than reworded, because mangling a doc comment to satisfy a scanner is the wrong direction.
